verdict.rationale: Aider is itself an official command-line tool. The docs cover installation, adding files on the aider command line, command-line switches with config-file and env-var equivalents, and non-interactive scripting via `--message`, which runs one instruction and exits. Community users corroborate using it interactively and in scriptable pipelines. Missing for 10: documented machine-readable (e.g. JSON) output or exit-code semantics for agentic automation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: Do this by naming them on the aider command line.
Aider takes a `--message` argument, where you can give it a natural language instruction. It will do that one thing, apply the edits to the files and then exit.
Aider has many options which can be set with command line switches.
aider --message "make a script that prints hello" hello.js
